title: The electric car of the future (1985)
caption:
Britain was promised the electric car of the future. It was a battery tricycle with a top speed of 24 km/h. 🔋
One small motor and one lead-acid battery: batteries lose capacity in the cold, and a small motor climbing a hill draws so much current that it overheats.
Ahead of its time or a death trap in a tracksuit: which was it?
first_comment: Honestly with a better battery this is just an e-scooter with a roof. Visionary or disaster? 🛵
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Sinclair C5': launched January 1985, a battery electric tricycle limited to 15 mph (24 km/h)

Wikipedia, 'Sinclair C5' (citing contemporary coverage): built by Hoover at its Merthyr Tydfil washing machine plant; a single lead-acid battery and motor; criticism of its low height in traffic, exposure to the weather, poor performance on hills and in cold weather (pedal assist); production cut within months; Sinclair Vehicles (renamed TPD) went into receivership in October 1985
